comparator.name: Latin American Studies
comparator.sourceNotes: The annual programme description expressly moves study abroad to the first semester of year two for September 2026 entrants. The annual curriculum table uses the earlier second-semester allocation and still places the ordinary 30 EC of taught courses in the first semester. The programme regulations launch the revised first year in 2026–2027. Eight components establish the 60 EC first year. The revised second-year taught course placement and later-year allocation are not confirmed for the new cohort. The 2026 regulations require the first-year diploma before study abroad, Research Methods and third-year electives. Research Methods precedes both the required noncredit thesis seminar and the thesis.

routeSelection.basis: The annual programme distinguishes a broad Spanish-speaking Latin America pathway and a Brazil/Portuguese pathway. The Spanish route provides the broader regional example for the generic target. Brazil/Portuguese remains a separate pathway.

exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Current workbook evidence identifies meaningful work in comparative history, politics, economics, qualitative research, media and art. Explicit regional examples include Mexican muralism within a global modern-art course and colonial exchanges with the Americas within a Renaissance course. The tested internally feasible composition remains a broad social-science and cultural-inquiry option. Final comparability depends on establishing the external entrant pathway.

candidateAssessment.concept: Latin American histories, societies and political economy
candidateAssessment.assessment: A workable internal 180 EC challenge connects comparative modern and imperial history, public policy, economics, qualitative inquiry, Indigenous histories and cultural analysis. Its advanced work remains broad or anchored elsewhere, without a sustained modern Latin American sequence. The final comparator judgment remains pending.

Psycholinguistics teaches language processing, acquisition and bilingualism, and stylistics analyzes language choices in texts. This does not provide repeated regional work on historical language varieties, contact, migration and identity. No full option is presented pending cohort verification.

candidateAssessment.concept: Latin American literature, film and popular culture
candidateAssessment.assessment: Film, adaptation and literary analysis offer tools for examining texts and images. Mexican muralism is one genuine regional topic within Modern Art and Modern Museums. Together the courses still center on comparative media and general cultural analysis, without sustained teaching in Latin American literature, film and popular culture. Final comparability remains pending.
